label: Consultant / Coach
rationale: A consultant's book is a handful of engagements, each sitting at a stage — scoping, in delivery, awaiting sign-off. The risk is never a missed hour, it is an engagement quietly parked at the same stage for five weeks. So the workspace opens on a docket like a law firm's, but sorted by stage rather than by deadline, so a column that has stopped moving is visible as a column. Underneath, the retainer hours drawn down, because that is the number that decides whether this month was profitable.

suppressed.reason: Consulting time is not chair time. A day of hourly lanes would show three calls and six hours of unstructured work the calendar never sees, which flatters the day and tells you nothing.
Same problem one grain out. The week is not the unit; the engagement is, and engagements run for months across a shifting set of days.
A consultant bills against a retainer, not a running balance. Draw-down is one figure in the metric row, and a debit-and-credit table would restate it at ten times the size.

surfaces.title: Engagements
surfaces.rationale: The book laid out ACROSS its stages rather than stacked down the page. A consultant reads left to right — scoping, out, in delivery, awaiting sign-off — and a stage that has stopped moving is only visible as a column with four things parked in it. In a vertical stack that finding disappears.

surfaces.title: Going quiet
surfaces.rationale: Retention risk never announces itself. It looks like replying later, skipping the homework, moving a session, getting vague about the goal. This is the consultant's version of the salon's rebooking leak, and it is only visible as an age-ranked list.

surfaces.title: Retainer
surfaces.rationale: Hours drawn against hours sold, and the work already done that has not been billed yet. Three figures in the same unit, no chart — this is a thing you check, not a thing you study.

surfaces.title: Capacity and pipeline
surfaces.rationale: This is two businesses at once — delivery and pipeline — and the dashboard has to hold both. Forward-looking capacity is what makes it different from every other vertical here: you cannot decide what to take on from a number that only describes last month.
